report:
Reviewed the complete claim, ordinary implementation association in spec.rs, and all six ordinary associated tests. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred prerequisites exist. Independently confirmed historical spec.rs and browser.rs snapshots match current bytes exactly; tests/spec.rs differs only in an unrelated review-inventory assertion adapting claim access to fragments (captured current lines). Historical approval rationale remains consistent with current evidence; it is not substituted for this assessment.

Implementation: explicit_anchor_end strips newline/CR and surrounding spaces/tabs, compares the entire HTML block line with the exact marker, and returns its start boundary. parse_anchors calls finish_anchor before that boundary; finish_anchor takes the active anchor, excluding the comment and preventing subsequent prose from entering it until a new definition sets active again. Other closure paths for headings, new definitions and document end require no explicit marker. HTML/code context guards preserve literal samples. All essential explicit-end behavior is in the associated spec.rs file.

Tests: exact_standalone_comments_end_content_and_allow_fresh_definitions asserts exact extracted claims and source spans for plain, padded and CRLF markers, intervening outside prose, and a new definition. malformed_looking_comments_are_content_and_do_not_end_claims asserts near-matches, trailing/prefix text and multiline comments remain content. claims_retain_all_blocks_until_the_next_definition_or_document_end verifies optional markers at definition/document boundaries through exact content and spans. every_atx_and_setext_heading_closes_content_until_a_new_definition verifies optional markers at every heading kind, excluding later outside prose. rendering_removes_only_parsed_end_markers verifies both rendering paths and exact removal spans while preserving literal examples and outside prose. prose_rendering_hides_control_comments_but_preserves_literal_examples adds HTML integration assertions distinguishing actual control comments from three escaped examples. These assertions would detect marker leakage, consuming outside prose, accepting near-matches, or requiring explicit closure at other boundaries. Captured source and BookFixture helpers show transparent fixture setup with assertions in test bodies.

This is a source adequacy review. I ran review start/read and byte/delta comparisons, then submitted this report with review record; I ran no functional tests or build. The coordinator separately reports 321 functional sage-meta tests and cargo build passing; that is reported baseline execution, not personal execution. No edits required.
